title: proofgate judges a heredoc's body only when it feeds a shell
intention: proofgate judges a heredoc's body as commands only when the heredoc feeds a shell, so writing a script that names a proof to a file passes unrewritten, while a heredoc fed to bash is still rewritten.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akienasus: `cat > $S/rec_ts.sh <<'EOF' ... timeout 900 python3 -u <proof> ... EOF; bin/cairn test --exec "$S/rec_ts.sh"` was rewritten to `cairn test --exec '<whole command>'`, because _segments cuts at newlines and judges the heredoc's body lines as shell segments. Writing a file runs nothing; the run went double-sealed.
traces_to: Law 4 (a gate that fires on data teaches the hand to route around it) and Law 8; dda0e72b9c67's census, whose heredoc spelling must stay rewritten.
how: In _verdict, before _segments, lift every heredoc body out of the command text: a line holding <<WORD / <<'WORD' / <<"WORD" / <<-WORD opens a body that runs to the line equal to WORD (tabs stripped for <<-), or to the end. The heredoc's command word is _command_word over the last segment of the text before << on its line. A shell word (SHELLS) judges the body by a nested _verdict at depth+1, as bash -c is; any other word leaves the body unjudged. Two teeth under this ticket's PROVES key, appended to _main.

clauses.claim: `cat > f <<'EOF'` and `tee f <<EOF` whose body holds a `python3 <proof>` line are judged None
`bash <<'EOS'`, `sh <<EOS` and `bash <<-EOS` with a `python3 <proof>` body are judged rewrite, and `bash <<EOF` with a `pytest` body is refused

decisions.text: D1: _verdict lifts heredoc bodies before cutting segments; a body feeding a shell is judged nested, any other body is data.
D2: two teeth, one per clause, under this ticket's PROVES key in the gate's proof, appended to _main.
